_comment: POSITION 7 tutorial scenario - The Danube Lesson, September 1805. Authored-deterministic: no variance bands (boot byte-identical under ANY seed), no navies (naval dormant), no agendas (deckless - AI-side survival only), no marshal_pool (no commissioning), no coalition. France + Bavaria (ALLIANCE - the transit bridge) vs Austria only; Austria at PEACE with Bavaria is WALLED by can_enter_territory (marches only - ATTACKS on a French army standing on Bavarian soil are legal, which is the free-play climax's own mechanism), so the front is one-way except the anchor corps authored forward. Player treasury 900 <= the EB-1 hoard floor 2000 (boot charges exactly 0). scenario_name is the ID the client's School of War overlay arms on - the pretty title lives in scenario_description. The four engine hint latches are authored true so engine one-shot popups never collide with tutor cards. Personality = character (MC-4): Mack is canonically LITERAL and belongs at Ulm, so the reserve pair here is ArchdukeCharles + Schwarzenberg (both cautious, values verbatim from europe_1805.json); Kienmayer holds Swabia as a LITERAL (MC-V-2: enemy literals play literal), while Jellacic is CAUTIOUS - the S5 live drive proved a literal's stagnation-breaker lunges him off the Tyrol anchor by turn 4, while a cautious defender fortifies the pass and STAYS (the T4 bombardment beat's anchor). Charles starts at HUNGARY, one march behind Vienna: the same drive saw a Vienna-paired reserve combine and sortie by turn 5 (44k onto the scripted beats' actors); starting them apart delays the combined-strength attack into the designed turn-8+ free-play window.
scenario_description: The Danube Lesson, September 1805. The Grande Armee wheels from the Channel to the Rhine. Austria has pushed two screening corps over the Iller; her main army musters at Vienna. A short, supervised campaign - Berthier keeps the school.

Ney.name: Ney

ability.name: Bravest of the Brave
ability.description: Ney's aggressive leadership inspires devastating attacks

Ney.biography: VI Corps on the Rhine - the bravest of the brave, first over every bridge. The Emperor keeps him on a short leash for the lesson.

Davout.name: Davout

ability.name: Iron Resolve
ability.description: The iron marshal coils behind his earthworks - patient discipline becomes a hammer-blow when III Corps springs
ability.effect: Each fortified turn builds +1 resolve stack (max 3). His next attack consumes all stacks for +8% each (max +24%). Stacks survive unfortify but clear if he moves or is routed.

Davout.biography: III Corps in its Lorraine camps - the iron marshal, whose books balance and whose sentries never sleep.

Soult.name: Soult

ability.name: Drillmaster of Boulogne
ability.description: Soult drilled the camps of Boulogne to clockwork - his corps sharpens in a single day
ability.effect: Drill completes in 1 turn (not 2) and never locks him out of your orders

Soult.biography: IV Corps, the depot army at Paris - a superb tactician who executes the Emperor's plan to the letter, exactly on the appointed hour.

Senarmont.name: Senarmont
Senarmont.biography: The Reserve Artillery - Senarmont's guns, which will one day roll to canister range at Friedland. For now they teach the trade.

Kienmayer.name: Kienmayer
Kienmayer.biography: An advance screen over the Iller, holding the ground it was given - to the letter, and no further.

Jellacic.name: Jellacic
Jellacic.biography: The mountain flank guard in the Tyrol passes - digging in where the ground is strongest.

ArchdukeCharles.name: ArchdukeCharles

ability.name: Habsburg Resolve
ability.description: Archduke Charles steadies the line with calm under fire

ArchdukeCharles.biography: The Habsburgs' best soldier, mustering the reserve on the Hungarian plain - he will come west when he is ready, and not an hour sooner.

Schwarzenberg.name: Schwarzenberg
Schwarzenberg.biography: The diplomat-soldier. Careful, patient, and impossible to provoke into a battle he has not already won.
